subject.title: cron: ghost runs recorded as ok when gateway is down (durationMs < 50ms)

question: Should OpenClaw accept the linked PR's defaulted config plus persisted protocol/UI warning surface for detecting fast main-session next-heartbeat cron handoffs, or should the fix be narrowed before merge?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the active fix adds operator-visible config and generated protocol/run-log surface, so automation should not choose the permanent product shape alone.

options.title: Refresh and decide the linked PR
options.body: Resolve the linked PR's merge/proof issues, then land it if maintainers accept the default-on warning/config/protocol shape.

options.title: Narrow the diagnostic surface
options.body: Replace or revise the linked PR to keep the ghost-run warning but remove or defer config/protocol/UI expansion that maintainers do not want yet.

options.title: Reject threshold-based detection
options.body: Close the linked PR and this issue only if maintainers decide duration-based ghost-run warnings are too heuristic for core cron behavior.

recommendation.title: Refresh and decide the linked PR
recommendation.body: Resolve the linked PR's merge/proof issues, then land it if maintainers accept the default-on warning/config/protocol shape.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter currently owns the sampled blame on both central cron/gateway paths and is the best available routing owner for the product-shape decision.
